title: Unconditional Action Practice
opening: You can choose an activity because it matters to you. Its result does not decide whether you matter.

example.activity: Write one private paragraph to explore an idea.

frames.label: Usual frame
frames.message: The paragraph must prove that I am brilliant.
frames.question: Notice pressure, attention, and enjoyment as they are now.

frames.label: Chosen action
frames.message: I choose to write one paragraph to explore an idea.
frames.question: Try one bounded, low-stakes action. Notice pressure, attention, and enjoyment.

example.standard: If you publish the paragraph, review its reasoning first.

limits.heading: Keep the task real
limits.body: A chosen action does not cancel a commitment or a standard that protects someone else. If removing a necessary check harms practical performance, restore that check.
limits.comparison: If pressure comes from an actual workload or deadline, address that condition too.

labels.frame: Choose a way to frame the action
labels.note: What did you notice about pressure, attention, or enjoyment? What task standard still applies?

feedback.missing: Write a note before you save it.
feedback.length: Your note is longer than 2,000 characters. Shorten it before you save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save did not finish. Your note is still here. Retry the save.
feedback.conflict: Another version was saved. Compare it with your note before you save again.
feedback.retryPending: Your last save did not finish. Retry the same save or keep your note here.
